jobs.title: Drift Wood #3 · the assembly
jobs.prompt: a four-panel comic strip laid out as a two-by-two grid on a half page, thin black panel borders (4 panels). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Cast, drawn the same in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 17, gaunt boy drawn a head too tall, oversized thrift-store wool overcoat to the knee worn indoors, faded black tee, dark jeans, sneakers, a bristol pad clutched flat to his chest, chin up; CHLOE — aged 17, girl with a sharp intelligent face, smudged heavy black eyeliner, straight dark hair to the shoulders, oversized dark cardigan, a Discman on her belt with headphones around her neck, a folded-back paperback, reads while talking; GULLY — aged 18, stocky boy with a round face, backwards blue cap, faded green hoodie with his hands in the front pocket, muddy tan work boots, easy slouch. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: Three hundred people, one direction, a man with a microphone and a plan for their futures. Panel 1: a high school gym assembly from the top of the bleachers, hundreds of students facing a principal at a microphone under a banner, three teenagers in the top row: a boy in an overcoat, a girl reading, a boy in a backwards cap drawing on his knee (in this panel: WOOD, CHLOE, GULLY). Principal says "...and every one of you has a future in this county.". Panel 2: close two-shot on a bleacher, a teenage boy leaning to whisper too loudly to a girl who keeps reading her paperback (in this panel: WOOD, CHLOE). Wood says "He said county. Not world. Not state. He looked at three hundred people and said county.". Chloe says "He's the principal, Wood. He's also in the county.". Panel 3: a teenage boy in a backwards cap holding up a notebook-paper drawing of a seagull at a microphone, grinning, bleachers behind (in this panel: GULLY). Gully says "Look. He's a gull.". Panel 4: a teenage boy in an overcoat looking with surprise at a drawing held by a boy in a backwards cap who is already drawing the next one, gym assembly below (in this panel: WOOD, GULLY). Wood says "...That's actually—". Gully says "Yeah.". Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized gull, two strokes. Reference @chloe_17 is the model sheet for CHLOE: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Reference @wood_20 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Match the attached references: @chloe_17 for the character the strip's Chloe at 17; @wood_20 for the character Wood at 20-23.
